subject: t14 round-1 findings against t5: role-name guard + atomic write, README copy-context/unpacked/serverName-bound/roles-pair corrections

findings_addressed.fix: `baseRosterRoleConflicts()` screens every derived role name with the runtime's own `registry.roleNameKey` against a key set built from the runtime's own roster table (`packages/mpd-roles-plugin/src/roles.data.ts`, the module `registry.ts` itself builds BASE_ROLE_NAME_KEYS from), and refuses with `registry.roleNameCollisionReason` (registry.ts:236-238) BEFORE anything is written. Measured: `scaffold plan` -> exit 1, stderr `refused — "plan" would declare a role name the base roster already owns` + `nothing was written to <target>`, stdout `refused: role name "plan reviewer" (contributes.roles[0] of extension "plan") is already taken by the base roster — this extension role is not exposed`, and the target directory does not exist afterwards (raw/refusal-plan.txt).

runScaffold now builds in a staging CONTAINER beside the target (`<parent>/.mpd-ext-scaffold-<pid>-<Date.now()>/<name>`), validates THAT tree with the runtime validator, and only then `renameSync`s the extension root onto the target (same filesystem, one atomic move). The container LEVEL is deliberate: discovery inspects only a root's immediate children for `mpd-ext.json`, so an extension staged one level down is never discoverable while it is being built. Any refusal removes the whole container in a `finally`, so a refused scaffold cannot leave a partially written extension. The old text `the generated extension does not load — this is a CLI defect` is gone: the post-validate failure path now reads `refused — the copy would not load as "<name>"; nothing was written to <target>` plus the per-item reasons. `grep -n "CLI defect" scripts/mpd-ext.mjs` returns only two COMMENTS that say the opposite (":227 instead of as a CLI defect.", ":396 a CONTRACT refusal, never a CLI defect").

selfTest section 4 covers the reachable collision id `plan` with six assertions: exit 1, the contract-refusal headline on stderr, the roster's own sentence on stdout, the `nothing was written` guarantee, no target directory, and no staging container left in the sandbox. `--self-test` is now 52 checks, exit 0.

Both template READMEs now say the template is deliberately NOT packed and state the consequence. MEASURED, and NARROWER THAN THE FINDING ASSUMED: the criterion said `validate`/`list` still work from a packed install, but the packer ships `packages/<pkg>/dist` and never `packages/<pkg>/src` (scripts/pack-mpd.mjs:69-73) while the CLI imports its validator from `src/`, so in a packed tree the CLI cannot run at all; with `src/` restored, `validate` runs and `scaffold` (plus `--self-test`'s template arm) fail on the absent template. Both arms are measured in raw/packed-tree-probe.json; the READMEs state the measured version.

Option B from the finding (location-neutral rewrite) was chosen over a third documented rewrite pass: the problematic sentences now describe `templates/mpd-extension/` as the upstream template directory and define "your copy" explicitly, and §6 says `templates/` is neither discovered nor packed while your copy is. §7 is retitled `The stdio MCP server (--with-mcp copies only)` and its smoke command uses `<extension-root>/server.mjs`. READMEs remain placeholder-free, so the t5 byte-comparison still holds (regression 39/39).

ONE helper pair now owns the bound: `serverNameMaxLength()` parses `{1,32}` out of `MPD_EXT_CONTRACT.serverNamePattern` (no literal 32 anywhere), and `serverNameFor(name)` is used by BOTH `finishManifest` and `compareCopyToTemplate`. A truncating id is no longer silent: runScaffold prints `warning: ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$ caps serverName at 32 characters, so the copy declares "…" instead of "…"` on stderr (new `warn()` helper, no exit-code change). `--self-test` 3b pins the behaviour with a 41-character id: exit 0, the declared serverName equals the 32-char bound, the warning is asserted, and the copy still validates (raw/long-id.txt).

The README's roles row now states the pair rule ("`provider`/`model` are optional and must be supplied together or not at all — the template keeps the default route, so it declares neither") in both languages. The template manifest itself is unchanged: it keeps the default route rather than pinning a provider into a copy-me skeleton.

The READMEs claimed the skill directory name must match the frontmatter name; that is wrong (the frontmatter `name` is the identity, the directory name is free — skills.ts reads the frontmatter, and the flow/skill rows in EXTENSIONS-FOR-AGENTS.md already said so). Both READMEs corrected in the same change.

honest_notes: The criterion's premise that `validate`/`list` work from a packed install does NOT hold as written; the probe measured the stronger fact (the CLI cannot run there at all). The READMEs and this record state the measured version, not the premise.

The `scaffold` refusal path still cannot prove that NO contract rule remains unchecked: the staging validator catches anything the pre-write guards miss, and reports it as a refusal with per-item reasons — but if such a case occurred the CLI would have no way to tell a hand-broken template from a bug, which is exactly why the headline says `refused` and names the target that was left untouched.
No dsh boot was run (no behaviour change to the plugin/runtime was made: this task touches the dev CLI and two README files only).
